0.en: Paul Harlan didn't wait for Jack to reach the door.
0.id: Paul Harlan tidak menunggu Jack sampai di pintu.

2.en: Lena shut off every nonessential industrial line last night. Yours was one of them.
2.id: Lena mematikan semua jalur industri yang tidak penting semalam. Punya Anda salah satunya.

3.id: Tidak ada yang bertanya pada saya.

4.en: Nobody asked anybody. It was the middle of the night and the town had just shrunk.
4.id: Tidak ada yang bertanya pada siapa pun. Itu tengah malam dan kota ini baru saja menyusut.

5.en: The technician beside Paul took the opportunity to slip back inside the building. Jack didn't blame him.
5.id: Teknisi di samping Paul memanfaatkan kesempatan itu untuk menyelinap kembali ke dalam gedung. Jack tidak menyalahkannya.

6.en: Paul jabbed a thumb over his shoulder, roughly toward the workshops.
6.id: Paul menyentakkan jempol ke belakang bahunya, kira-kira ke arah bengkel-bengkel.

7.en: My lathes run on coolant. Coolant is water. Half my machines are sitting there with jobs clamped in them, and if they sit dry long enough, I'm going to lose parts I can't make again. Not with what's left in this town.
7.id: Mesin bubut saya jalan pakai cairan pendingin. Cairan pendingin itu air. Separuh mesin saya diam di sana dengan benda kerja masih terjepit, dan kalau dibiarkan kering cukup lama, saya bakal kehilangan suku cadang yang tidak bisa saya buat lagi. Tidak dengan apa yang tersisa di kota ini.

8.en: How much water do you need?
8.id: Berapa banyak air yang Anda butuhkan?

9.en: Paul opened his mouth, then closed it again. He clearly hadn't expected that question.
9.id: Paul membuka mulut, lalu menutupnya lagi. Jelas ia tidak menyangka pertanyaan itu.

11.en: Then tell Lena. She'll put it on the list. But I'm going to be honest with you, it won't be at the top.
11.id: Kalau begitu bilang ke Lena. Dia akan memasukkannya ke daftar. Tapi saya mau jujur dengan Anda, itu tidak akan ada di urutan teratas.

13.en: Sarah answered from the vehicle, where Mark was helping her out.
13.id: Sarah yang menjawab dari kendaraan, tempat Mark sedang membantunya turun.

14.en: Below drinking, below medical, below cooking. Above washing cars.
14.id: Di bawah air minum, di bawah medis, di bawah memasak. Di atas cuci mobil.

15.en: Paul looked at her, then at the careful way she was standing, then back at Jack. Some of the anger went out of his shoulders. Not all of it.
15.id: Paul memandangnya, lalu cara hati-hati Sarah berdiri, lalu kembali ke Jack. Sebagian amarah luruh dari bahunya. Tidak semuanya.

16.en: I'm not trying to steal anybody's drinking water.
16.id: Saya tidak sedang berusaha mencuri air minum siapa pun.

18.en: My night shift was on the floor when that machine went off. They didn't get home in time to fill any bathtubs. They're going to get the same slow faucet as everybody else, and some of their neighbors are going to be sitting on a bathtub full of water.
18.id: Sif malam saya sedang di lantai bengkel waktu mesin itu menyala. Mereka tidak sempat pulang untuk mengisi bak mandi. Mereka bakal dapat keran pelan yang sama seperti semua orang, sementara sebagian tetangga mereka duduk di samping bak mandi penuh air.

19.en: Jack hadn't thought about that. He looked at Sarah, and could see she hadn't either.
19.id: Jack belum memikirkan hal itu. Ia memandang Sarah, dan bisa melihat Sarah juga belum.

20.en: Come inside. You should hear the numbers.

22.en: The utility station was all concrete and pipe and humming machinery, warm in a way that the rest of the town hadn't been all morning. Lena was already there, standing in front of a wall of round brass gauges with a tablet in one hand, a pen in her teeth, and her hair tied back in a knot that had clearly been redone several times since eleven o'clock.
22.id: Stasiun utilitas itu serba beton dan pipa dan mesin yang berdengung, hangat dengan cara yang tak dirasakan bagian kota lainnya sepanjang pagi. Lena sudah ada di sana, berdiri di depan dinding penuh alat ukur kuningan yang bundar dengan tablet di satu tangan, pulpen di antara giginya, dan rambut diikat cepol yang jelas sudah diikat ulang beberapa kali sejak pukul sebelas.

23.en: She took the pen out of her mouth.

24.en: Oh good, everybody. Sit down, Sarah.
24.id: Wah, bagus, semuanya datang. Duduk, Sarah.

27.en: Sarah sat in the nearest chair. Mark leaned in the doorway, as he did in every doorway, as though doorways were his natural habitat.
27.id: Sarah duduk di kursi terdekat. Mark bersandar di ambang pintu, seperti di setiap ambang pintu, seolah ambang pintu adalah habitat alaminya.

28.id: Lena mengetuk alat ukur yang paling besar.

29.en: Two main tanks. Drinking water. When they're full, they hold about five hundred thousand liters together. Plus the fire reserve, which nobody touches unless something's burning.
29.id: Dua tangki utama. Air minum. Kalau penuh, keduanya menampung sekitar lima ratus ribu liter. Ditambah cadangan pemadam kebakaran, yang tidak disentuh siapa pun kecuali ada yang terbakar.

32.en: It would be, if they were full. They weren't. They're never full at night.
32.id: Memang banyak, kalau penuh. Tadi tidak penuh. Tangkinya tidak pernah penuh di malam hari.

33.en: She drew a curve on her tablet and held it up.
33.id: Ia menggambar sebuah kurva di tabletnya dan mengangkatnya.

34.en: We use water all day. The tanks drop. Then every night, between midnight and five, they refill from the reservoir.
34.id: Kita memakai air sepanjang hari. Isi tangki turun. Lalu setiap malam, antara tengah malam dan jam lima, tangki diisi ulang dari waduk.

35.en: Jack saw it before she said it.
35.id: Jack sudah melihatnya sebelum Lena mengatakannya.

36.en: And TOMBS cut the intake at eleven.
36.id: Dan TOMBS memutus saluran masuknya jam sebelas.

37.en: At eleven. Right before the refill. The tanks were close to the lowest they ever get.
37.id: Jam sebelas. Tepat sebelum pengisian ulang. Tangkinya sedang hampir di titik terendah yang pernah dicapainya.

38.en: Sarah leaned forward in her chair.

39.en: How much is in them now?

40.en: Lena checked the gauge, then her tablet, then the gauge again, as if the second look might change the answer.
40.id: Lena memeriksa alat ukur, lalu tabletnya, lalu alat ukur lagi, seolah lirikan kedua bisa mengubah jawabannya.

41.en: About three hundred and fifty thousand liters. After this morning.
41.id: Sekitar tiga ratus lima puluh ribu liter. Setelah pagi ini.

43.en: That still sounds like a lot.

44.en: Normal use is about a hundred thousand a day. Showers, laundry, cooking, the greenhouse, the shops. Everything.
44.id: Pemakaian normal sekitar seratus ribu sehari. Mandi, cucian, memasak, rumah kaca, bengkel-bengkel. Semuanya.

45.en: The room was quiet for a moment.

46.en: Paul did the math out loud, the way people do when they want someone to tell them they've done it wrong.
46.id: Paul menghitungnya keras-keras, seperti orang yang berharap ada yang bilang hitungannya salah.

49.en: Jack looked at the gauges. Half a dozen needles, steady, unremarkable, telling the whole town how long it had.
49.id: Jack memandang alat-alat ukur itu. Setengah lusin jarum, diam, biasa saja, memberi tahu seluruh kota berapa lama waktu yang tersisa.

50.en: So we don't use water normally.
50.id: Jadi kita tidak memakai air dengan normal.

52.en: Emergency guidance says a person can get by on about twenty liters a day. Drinking, cooking, a little washing. That's not comfortable. But it's enough.
52.id: Pedoman darurat bilang satu orang bisa bertahan dengan sekitar dua puluh liter sehari. Minum, memasak, sedikit mencuci. Itu tidak nyaman. Tapi cukup.

53.en: Jack ran it in his head.

55.en: Ten thousand liters a day for homes. Medical needs its own, about three thousand. The kitchens, another two. Call it fifteen thousand a day. Toilets get flushed with a bucket of used washing water, not from the faucet.
55.id: Sepuluh ribu liter sehari untuk rumah-rumah. Bagian medis butuh jatah sendiri, sekitar tiga ribu. Dapur, dua ribu lagi. Anggap saja lima belas ribu sehari. Toilet disiram pakai seember air bekas cucian, bukan dari keran.

57.en: That leaves the greenhouse. Aiden irrigates every morning.
57.id: Tinggal rumah kaca. Aiden menyiram setiap pagi.

58.en: From the drinking tanks. It's a big piece of normal use. Bigger than the kitchens.
58.id: Dari tangki air minum. Itu bagian besar dari pemakaian normal. Lebih besar daripada dapur.

59.en: Paul spoke up without being asked.

60.en: Then don't use drinking water for it.
60.id: Kalau begitu jangan pakai air minum untuk itu.

62.en: The wastewater plant treats everything that goes down the drains, doesn't it? Not to drinking quality. But clean enough for plants.
62.id: Instalasi air limbah mengolah semua yang masuk ke saluran pembuangan, kan? Bukan sampai layak minum. Tapi cukup bersih untuk tanaman.

64.en: It does. The treated water goes out to a holding tank and gets released.
64.id: Betul. Air olahannya dialirkan ke tangki penampung lalu dibuang.

65.en: Then stop releasing it. Run a line from that tank to the greenhouse irrigation. I can make you the fittings. My night shift can lay the pipe.
65.id: Kalau begitu berhenti membuangnya. Pasang jalur dari tangki itu ke irigasi rumah kaca. Saya bisa buatkan sambungannya. Sif malam saya bisa memasang pipanya.

67.en: That would take the greenhouse off the drinking water entirely.
67.id: Dengan begitu rumah kaca sama sekali lepas dari air minum.

68.en: Give me my night shift and a day.
68.id: Beri saya sif malam saya dan satu hari.

69.en: Jack looked at Paul for a long moment. It was the same man who, earlier that morning, had stood up in front of the whole town and asked who had done this to them.
69.id: Jack memandang Paul lama. Ini laki-laki yang sama yang pagi tadi berdiri di depan seluruh kota dan bertanya siapa yang telah melakukan ini pada mereka.

70.en: You'll have them. And your coolant goes on the list.
70.id: Anda akan mendapatkannya. Dan cairan pendingin Anda masuk daftar.

71.en: Paul nodded once, and didn't say thank you, and didn't need to.
71.id: Paul mengangguk sekali, dan tidak mengucapkan terima kasih, dan memang tidak perlu.

72.en: Sarah did the last of it in her head faster than anyone.
72.id: Sarah menghitung sisanya di kepala lebih cepat daripada siapa pun.

73.en: Fifteen thousand a day. Twenty-three days.
73.id: Lima belas ribu sehari. Dua puluh tiga hari.

74.en: A little over three weeks. If nothing leaks. If nothing breaks. If nobody cheats.
74.id: Sedikit lebih dari tiga minggu. Kalau tidak ada yang bocor. Kalau tidak ada yang rusak. Kalau tidak ada yang curang.

77.en: Then a little less than three weeks.
77.id: Kalau begitu sedikit kurang dari tiga minggu.

78.en: Jack turned it over. Three weeks was not forever. But three weeks was not three days, either. It was time to think. Time to try things.
78.id: Jack menimbangnya. Tiga minggu bukan selamanya. Tapi tiga minggu juga bukan tiga hari. Itu waktu untuk berpikir. Waktu untuk mencoba berbagai hal.

79.en: Sarah tapped the arm of her chair.

80.en: That leaves Paul's night shift. And everyone else who didn't fill a bathtub.
80.id: Tinggal sif malam Paul. Dan semua orang lain yang tidak mengisi bak mandi.

81.en: Mark sounded like he already knew the answer.
81.id: Mark terdengar seolah sudah tahu jawabannya.

82.en: Can we take the water back?

84.en: Knock on five hundred doors and tell people to drain their bathtubs into a truck? We'd lose more trust than water.
84.id: Mengetuk lima ratus pintu dan menyuruh orang menguras bak mandi mereka ke truk? Kita bakal kehilangan lebih banyak kepercayaan daripada air.

86.en: Sarah thought about it, chin resting on her hand.
86.id: Sarah memikirkannya, dagu bertumpu di tangan.

87.en: We don't take it. It's theirs. Whatever's already in a bathtub or a bucket is that household's own. But nobody gets more than twenty liters a day from the faucets, whether they filled a bathtub or not. And we put a drinking-water point at the community center, where anyone who runs short can fill a jug. No questions. Just their name in a book.
87.id: Kita tidak mengambilnya. Itu milik mereka. Apa pun yang sudah ada di bak mandi atau ember adalah milik rumah tangga itu sendiri. Tapi tidak ada yang dapat lebih dari dua puluh liter sehari dari keran, entah mereka mengisi bak mandi atau tidak. Dan kita buka titik air minum di balai warga, tempat siapa pun yang kekurangan bisa mengisi jeriken. Tanpa pertanyaan. Cukup tulis nama di buku.

89.en: So the people who filled their tubs got ahead.
89.id: Jadi orang-orang yang mengisi bak mandi mereka jadi lebih unggul.

90.en: For a few days. After that, everybody's the same.
90.id: Untuk beberapa hari. Setelah itu, semua orang sama.

92.en: No. It's just less unfair than anything else we could do this morning.
92.id: Memang tidak. Cuma kurang tidak adil dibanding apa pun yang bisa kita lakukan pagi ini.

93.en: He thought about it, then shrugged.

94.en: My guys can live with that.
94.id: Anak buah saya bisa terima itu.

95.en: Lena wrote it all down in a hand that got smaller and faster as she went.
95.id: Lena mencatat semuanya dengan tulisan yang makin kecil dan makin cepat.

96.en: Two supply windows a day. An hour in the morning, an hour in the evening. Full pressure during those windows, a trickle the rest of the time. Twenty liters a person. Medical and kitchens on their own allowance. Toilets flushed with washing water. Greenhouse on treated water once Paul's line is in. Drinking point at the community center.
96.id: Dua sesi pasokan sehari. Satu jam pagi, satu jam sore. Tekanan penuh selama sesi itu, tetesan kecil di luar itu. Dua puluh liter per orang. Medis dan dapur dapat jatah sendiri. Toilet disiram pakai air cucian. Rumah kaca pakai air olahan begitu jalur Paul terpasang. Titik air minum di balai warga.

97.en: It took the rest of the morning to turn all of it into rules. Lena called medical and the kitchens for their real numbers. Paul walked the greenhouse lines and came back with a list of parts. Sarah argued with the wording from her chair until it said exactly what it meant, and nothing it didn't.
97.id: Butuh sisa pagi itu untuk mengubah semuanya menjadi aturan. Lena menelepon bagian medis dan dapur untuk angka mereka yang sebenarnya. Paul menyusuri jalur-jalur rumah kaca dan kembali dengan daftar suku cadang. Sarah memperdebatkan susunan kalimatnya dari kursinya sampai bunyinya persis seperti maksudnya, dan tidak lebih.

98.en: Lena looked up from the final draft.

99.id: Sekarang jam sebelas lima puluh dua.

102.en: Lena walked to the console in the corner, the one that tied into every speaker in the settlement, and opened the channel. Her voice went out across the whole town, calm and plain and almost bored, the voice of someone reading a bus timetable.
102.id: Lena berjalan ke konsol di sudut, yang tersambung ke setiap pengeras suara di permukiman, dan membuka kanalnya. Suaranya menyebar ke seluruh kota, tenang dan polos dan nyaris bosan, suara seseorang yang sedang membacakan jadwal bus.

103.en: She read the limits once, slowly. Then she read them again.
103.id: Ia membacakan batasannya sekali, pelan-pelan. Lalu ia membacakannya sekali lagi.

104.en: When she closed the channel, the station was quiet except for the hum of the pumps.
104.id: Ketika ia menutup kanal, stasiun itu hening kecuali dengung pompa.

105.en: Sarah wasn't looking at the gauges anymore. She was looking past them, out the small, high window on the station's far wall, where a slice of the morning sky showed between two pipes. Above the rooftops beyond it, the tips of the grass moved in a breeze they couldn't feel through the concrete.
105.id: Sarah tak lagi memandangi alat-alat ukur. Ia memandang melewatinya, ke jendela kecil yang tinggi di dinding seberang stasiun, tempat seiris langit pagi tampak di antara dua pipa. Di atas atap-atap di baliknya, ujung-ujung rumput bergerak tertiup angin yang tak bisa mereka rasakan menembus beton.

110.en: That's what we're supposed to be counting.
110.id: Memang itu yang harus kita hitung.

111.en: I know. But we're only counting the water inside.
111.id: Aku tahu. Tapi kita cuma menghitung air yang ada di dalam.

112.en: Jack followed her eyes to the window, to the grass. Then he remembered the southern edge in the dark, and a bead of water clinging under a blade, rising nearly to his chest.
112.id: Jack mengikuti arah pandangnya ke jendela, ke rumput. Lalu ia teringat tepian selatan dalam gelap, dan sebutir air yang menggantung di bawah sehelai rumput, tingginya nyaris sampai ke dadanya.

113.en: Last night. At the edge. There was a drop of water out there as tall as I am to the ribs.
113.id: Semalam. Di tepian. Ada setetes air di luar sana yang tingginya sampai ke rusukku.

115.id: Satu tetes. Di satu helai rumput.

116.en: She looked back at the window.

117.en: How many blades are out there, Jack?
117.id: Ada berapa helai rumput di luar sana, Jack?
